name: Iqpill

lead: The iqpill is a term used on looksmaxxing forums for the view that intelligence matters at least as much as appearance for success, status and attraction. It is discussed as a counterpart to the "looks" side of the community: if looks are one lever, cognitive ability is another.

Discussion is mostly opinion and personal anecdote. Threads ask how to measure IQ, whether it can be raised, and how it compares with traits such as metacognition. No dating-specific research is cited in the threads themselves.

paras: In practice the iqpill is a way of framing priorities rather than a routine. Forum members compare themselves with peers on perceived intelligence, trade views on online IQ tests, and debate whether IQ can be raised or is fixed. Some members argue that skills such as metacognition, communicating succinctly and learning deliberately can add to how capable and attractive a person comes across.

There is no physical risk. Community posts show that some members describe feeling distressed about their own perceived intelligence, and online IQ tests discussed in the threads are not clinical assessments. Members disagree with one another on whether IQ is changeable.

angle.text: Proponents treat intelligence as a way to improve overall attractiveness and standing without changing physical features. Members mention metacognition and succinct communication as skills that can show up in conversation and first impressions.

lead: The iqpill is slang on looksmaxxing forums for the idea that intelligence gives a person an edge in life and in dating that is independent of physical appearance. [1]

Members use it to set looks against other assets. One thread poster calls IQ "the most important metric in life" while others in the same threads dismiss it, and a separate thread argues that metacognition, the ability to reflect on one's own thinking, matters more than raw IQ. [2]

Related threads ask how to take reliable IQ tests and whether IQ can be increased; one reply states flatly that it cannot be. [1] The discussion is anecdotal, and the threads do not point to published studies.
infobox: Intelligence as an asset alongside looks

paras: "Iqpill" refers to the belief that cognitive ability confers advantages in work, status and relationships on top of, or instead of, physical looks. It appears in thread titles that treat having a high or average IQ as a major life variable. [1][2]

One poster describes average IQ as a position of awareness without the ability to keep up with quicker thinkers, and compares IQ to "firmware" that can be polished but not replaced. Another reply in the same thread calls IQ cope, showing the community is split. [3]

A different thread claims metacognition outranks raw IQ, arguing that people with high IQ and poor self-monitoring become overconfident, while lower-IQ people with good self-monitoring know when they do not know something. [2]

The term shows up beside "succinctnesspill", suggesting the community also groups communication style with intelligence as traits that shape how people are perceived. [4] Questions about raising IQ draw replies ranging from "you can always increase it" to "can't". [1]

lore.intro: On looksmaxxing forums the iqpill is debated as one of several variables, with members disagreeing on how large and how changeable it is. [1][3]
